timing.note: First-order mechanics (inertia + viscous and Coulomb friction) integrated every 1 ms of virtual time; winding inductance (electrical time constant ≈ 1 ms) is ignored.

analog.note: Linear DC motor: back-EMF = Ke·ω in series with the winding resistance, Ke/Kt/friction derived from the rated voltage, no-load speed, stall and no-load current. Under fast PWM (an L298N output while ENA gets analogWrite) the winding is duty-averaged assuming continuous current: I = (duty·V_on − Ke·ω)/R, so speed ≈ duty × full speed, and the battery supplies duty·I. Real drivers in fast-decay mode with a light load can run faster than that at low duty, and below ~20–30 % duty a real TT motor often does not start under load.

power.note: Draws its real current from the driver and the battery (stall ≈ 1.5 A at 6 V), so supply sag and driver overcurrent show up; heating and brush losses are not modelled.

emulates: Speed proportional to average voltage minus friction
Spin-up and coast-down with a time constant
Start-up dead band from static friction
doesNotEmulate: Unit-to-unit spread (real TT motors differ by ±10–20 % in speed, which makes a robot curve)
testOnRealDevice: Whether both motors run at the same speed (calibrate a per-motor PWM trim)
Minimum PWM that starts the motor under load
Supply brown-out on the Arduino when motors start (use a separate battery for the motors)
